introduction: The protocol aims to guide a future systematic review asking what the effects of aerobic exercise are on reducing depression levels in adults. It is meant to give researchers and healthcare professionals a rigorous and transparent methodological foundation.
methodology: The paper is a protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials, following PRISMA-P 2020. Six databases will be searched with MeSH-based descriptors. Two researchers will select studies independently. Quality will be assessed with TESTEX and RoB 2.0, and certainty with GRADE. Participants will be adults with depression.
theory: The protocol says it will follow the PRISMA-P guidelines; no theory is named.
results: The paper is a protocol and reports no results.
discussion: The authors expect the review to identify the most effective dose-response for reducing depression levels. They also expect it to offer in-depth understanding of the mechanisms through which aerobic exercise influences depression.
limitations: The authors list anticipated limitations: small sample sizes, lack of clarity about the mechanisms of exercise's effect on depression, and varied intensity protocols. They expect high heterogeneity among the studies to be included.

introduction.q: This protocol proposal aims to guide a future systematic review that will seek to answer the following question: what are the effects of aerobic exercise on reducing depression levels in adults?

we intend to provide researchers and healthcare professionals with a rigorous and transparent methodological foundation for conducting a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials on the topic.

methodology.q: This is a systematic review protocol, which will follow the PRISMA-P 2020 guidelines and has been registered in PROSPERO (no. CRD42024592700).
The study search will be conducted in six databases: BVS, Cochrane library, Embase, Epistemonikos, PubMed and SPORTDiscus, using MeSH-based descriptors.
Studies will be selected independently by two researchers
Participants will include adults (>18 years) diagnosed with depression
the risk of bias will be evaluated using the Cochrane RoB 2.0 method
the methodological quality of studies on physical exercise will be assessed with the TESTEX tool
The certainty of evidence will be evaluated through the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE).
The effect models (fixed or random) will be used to estimate the treatment effect (aerobic exercise) for depression in adults.

theory.q: The study is a protocol for a systematic review, which will follow the guidelines developed by Page et al. known as the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA-P) for systematic reviews

results.q: This is a systematic review protocol, which will follow the PRISMA-P 2020 guidelines

discussion.q: to identify the most effective dose-response for this reduction
the review is expected to offer in-depth understanding of the biological and psychological mechanisms through which aerobic exercise influences depression levels

limitations.q: Anticipated limitations and challenges include the following issues: the use of small sample sizes, lack of clarity regarding the specific mechanisms through which exercise contributes to the improvement of depression, and variations in the intensity protocols adopted.
one of the main methodological challenges expected in the conduction of this review is the high heterogeneity among the studies to be included
The systematic review studies conducted so far, although following rigorous methodologies and providing relevant contributions to the scientific field, present some methodological limitations.

abstract_claims.q: Studies suggest that aerobic exercise can improve mental health and reduce depression symptoms, despite variations in exercise type and intensity.

It is expected that the systematic review following this protocol will identify the effective dose-response to reduce depression levels and provide an understanding of the mechanisms through which aerobic exercise influences depression.

caveats.q: Although the benefits of aerobic exercise in improving depressive symptoms are well documented, the existing literature shows high variability in terms of modality, intensity, frequency, and duration of exercise.
Furthermore, the underlying mechanisms of these effects are still not fully understood
However, the analysis of these exercises should not be based solely on perceived effort or heart rate
